post.description:
To select the subscribers to be exported, you will need a target. This target can be created in the mail applilcation or by [api](api/#operation/Targets_Post).
             📝 The default output file is an ANSI encoded csv file with ";" as column separator and CRLF windows newline character. Field names are used for column headers.
             📝 The execution of the export is asynchronous, so you won't know right away if the export is successful. But in case of error, you will receive en email "Error concerning the export...".
             At the end of the export, you will also receive an email with the subject starting with "Export of the file..."
             ⚠️ Be careful, if you run too many exports at the same time, you'll get this error : "Error, too many exports in progress (max 10)". For performance reasons, we don't allow more than 10 simultaneous exports per database.
             💡 You can call this [endpoint](#operation/Exports_LastExportStatus) to get the execution status of your export you just created.

delete.description:
Same behaviour as the DELETE /subscribers method, except the subscriber identifiers are sent in the request body instead of the query string.
Use this method for large deletions: a long list of identifiers in the url exceeds the maximum query string length and makes the request fail.
The body is a plain json array of integers, for example [12,45,4789]. 5000 identifiers max per call.
The method returns the identifiers that were actually deleted. If an identifier is not found, it is not present in the result array.
⚠️ Do not use this method to delete all your subscribers! It won't be effective! If you want to delete millions of rows, you can ask customer service.

post.summary: Method to unsubscribe e-mail addresses from newsletters
post.description:
This method is useful to unsubscribe your subscribers.
📝 You can unsubscribe in 3 ways:
- from the global newsletter :
- subscriber_status = optin (field[7]=1)
- unsubscription_date = Now (field[4]=Now)
- from partner offers:
- Partner offers opt-in = Yes (field[8]=1)
- Partner offers opt-in date = Now (field[10]=Now)
- from a specific newsletter
- field[IdSubscriptionField] = 1
- field[IdUnsubDateField] = Now

💡 This method should be use to manage your unsubscriptions because it updates the unsubscription statistics of your campaigns. To do this, you must enter the IdSent parameter which you can retrieve using the config tag [[CONF.7]]

put.summary: Method to subscribe existing e-mail addresses to newsletter
put.description:
This method is useful for subscribing or resubscribing an email that has already been subscribed to in the past. Thus the origin of the collect (stored in the date of first subscription and first origin fields) is not overwritten.
📝 This method updates the following fields :
- field[7]=0 (subscriber_status=optin)
- field[3]=Date (last subscription date)
- field[6]=LastOrigin (last provenance)
- if SubscribeToPartnersOffers=True, field[8]=1 (Partner offers opt-in = Yes)
- if SubscribeToPartnersOffers=True, field[10]=Date (partners offers optin date)

The method returns a boolean array indicating if update has been done for each subscriber id.

post.summary: Method to subscribe new e-mail addresses to newsletter
post.description:
This method is useful to subscribe a new inserted email addresses with its origin information (stored in the date of first subscription and first origin fields) .
📝 This method updates the following fields :
- field[7]=0 (subscriber_status=optin)
- field[2]=field[3]=Date (first & last subscription dates)
- field[5]=field[6]=FirstOrigin (first and last provenance)
- field[21]=collectMode - field[22]= collectType - if SubscribeToPartnersOffers = True, field[8]=1 (Partner offers opt-in = Yes)
- if SubscribeToPartnersOffers = True, field[10]=Date (partners offers optin date)

The method returns a boolean array indicating if update has been done for each subscriber id.

operator.description:
Operator to use:
  • 1 = **"HasValue"** : The field has a value (the "Value" parameter is not used with this operator)
  • 2 = **"NoValue"** : The field has no value (the "Value" parameter is not used with this operator)
  • 3 = **"Equals"** : The field equals a value 💡 You can combine several values by separating them with a ";". A logical OR will be applied between the values. 💡 You can use the wildcard * with string values. E.g webmail (field[37]) equal to "hotmail.*"
  • 4 = **"DifferentThan"** : The field is different than a value 💡 You can combine several values by separating them with a ";". A logical OR will be applied between the values.
  • 5 = **"LessThan"** : The field is strictly lower than a value (for Number and Date type only)
  • 6 = **"MoreThan"** : The field is strictly greater than a value (for Number and Date type only)
  • 7 = **"Between"** : The field is between two (included) values separated with a pipe ('|') (for Number and Date type only)
  • 8 = **"DatePast"** : The value of the date field must correspond to a past date calculated from today (for type Date only). Value format is nbDays|nbMonths|nbYears, with nbDays, nbMonths, and nbYears as optional. ⚠️ Value "-1" is used to store a null value 📝 The operator works as follows: First, we calculate the past date as follow : PastDate = TODAY - nbDays - nbMonths - nbYears Then, the subscriber date field must follow these criteria: - if nbDays is specified (≥0), the day part of the PastDate must be equal to the day part of the subscriber date field, - if nbMonths is specified (≥0), the month part of the PastDate must be equal to the month part of the subscriber date field, - if nbYears is specified (≥0), the year part of the PastDate must be equal to the year part of the subscriber date field. e.g "-1|-1|1" means "any day of the month of the last year " "0|0|1" means "the same day of the month of the last year" "0|0|0" means "today" "0|0|-1" means "same day and same month (and any year)" = "is birthday" "1|0|0" means "yesterday" "0|1|0" means "the same day of the last month" "-1|1|0" means "any day of the last month"
  • 9 = **"DateFuture"** : The value of the date field must correspond to a future date calculated from today (for type Date only). Value format is nbDays|nbMonths|nbYears, with nbDays, nbMonths, and nbYears as optional. ⚠️ Value "-1" is used to store a null value 📝The operator works as follows: First, we calculate the future date as follow : FutureDate = TODAY + nbDays + nbMonths + nbYears Then, the subscriber date field must follow these criteria: - if nbDays is specified (≥0), the day part of the FutureDate must be equal to the day part of the subscriber date field, - if nbMonths is specified (≥0), the month part of the FutureDate must be equal to the month part of the subscriber date field, - if nbYears is specified (≥0), the year part of the FutureDate must be equal to the year part of the subscriber date field. e.g "-1|-1|1" means "any day of the month of the next year " "0|0|1" means "the same day of the month of the next year" "0|0|0" means "today" "0|0|-1" means "same day and same month (and any year)" = "is birthday" "1|0|0" means "tomorrow" "0|1|0" means "the same day of the next month" "-1|1|0" means "any day of the next month"
  • 10 = **"NbDaysMoreThan"** : More than X days ago (for Date type only) 📝 The subscriber date value must be newer than X days ago. So the formula used is : SubscriberFieldDate > (NOW - X DAYS)
  • 11 = **"NbDaysLessThan"** : Less than X days ago (for type Date only) (for Date type only) 📝 The subscriber date value must older than X days ago. So the formula used is : SubscriberFieldDate < (NOW - X DAYS)
  • 12 = **"AgeGreaterThan"** : The age in years is greater than the specified value (for type Date only)
  • 13 = **"AgeLesserThan"** : The age in years is less than the specified value (for type Date only)
  • 14 = **"AgeBetween"** : The age in years is between two specified values separated with a pipe ('|') (for type Date only)

TargetFileFilter.description:
Structure for saving the filter by file of a standard target.
Filter by file allows you to target a defined population in a file by list of emails, of IDs, or even of postcodes.
In this type of filter you must therefore specify the record name to be used and the base field against which to map the data.
            
Before using this type of filter, you must put your file on the MindBaz FTP. If you do not have access, you can request an access to the MindBaz customer services.
The file might be in a sub-directories.
Attention: The file should be in ANSI format and should only contain one column without a header and without a text identifier.
Attention: A target does not import e-mail addresses from the file. Email addresses should exists in the database.

isEnabled.description: Indicates if the filter is active.

filename.description: Name of the file (may contain a sub-directory, eg: "my-sub-dir\my-file.csv"

dbFieldName.description:
Database field name on which the data in the file will be mapped.
Works as follows : "fld" + field identifier
Example:
- fld0 for subscriber ID
- fld1 for e-mail address
- fld18 for post codes
- (exception)  md5_fld1 for e-mail addresses encrypted in md5 (md5 must be activated by the MindBaz customer service on demand).

fileAutomaticDeletionDate.description: (Mandatory)Date of automatic deletion of the file on ftp.

ImportMapping.description:
Records the mapping of a file column in a db field.
Also records the addition of a fixed value within a db field (this fixed value may be used for all lines in the file).
This class is used in the ImportParameter class in a table which contains the mapping for all file columns to be imported

dbFieldName.description:
Name of the field within the db.
15 carac max.
e.g.
fld1 for e-mail address
fld2 for first subscription date
etc.
\attention Mandatory field

idMappingMode.description:
Mapping mode ID
1 (default): overwrite (file data overwrites db data - unless file data is nil)
2: retain (file data is written only if db data is nil)
\attention Mandatory field

name of file column mapped to dbFieldName.

255 carac max

fixedValue.description:
Fixed value mapped to dbFieldName.
Date format to be used "dd/MM/yyyy".
May not be used with the fileColumnName field.
1000 carac max
\attention Mandatory field is fileColumnName is nil

format.description:
Date format of the file column.
For information only on mapping of a column (fileColumnName) of DATE or LIST type.
Example of DATE format: "dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm:ss", "yyyy-MM-dd", "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss", ...
For a LIST type, choose from 2 format options: "ID or "VALUE"
    ID: the file data for this column corresponds to the list ID (e.g. "0","1" for the list "0:No,1:Yes")
    VALUE: the file data for this column corresponds to list values ( e.g. "No","Yes" for list "0:No,1:Yes").
For other types, this field should be left blank.
30 carac max

tags.name: Targets
tags.description:
Service managing emailing targets. An emailing target allows you to select subscribers from your MINDBAZ database according to several criteria (called filters):
  • Field filter (e.g. webmail, gender, age, is optin, etc.)
  • Behaviour filter (e.g. clicked 2 times in the last 30 days)
  • Thematic filter (e.g. opened at least 3 times in the last 20 days a campaign with the theme Travel)
  • Sending filter (e.g. has received one or several sendings)
  • Email pressure filter (e.g. Has been targeted at least 2 times during this week)
  • Geoloc filter (e.g. live in France under 10km from postal code 59000)
  • SQL filter (you can write your own Sql query)
  • File filter (e.g. target subscribers whose email address is present in a file)
📝 A target can be used to :
  • select the subscribers who will receive your email campaign. More information [here](#operation/Segments_Post)
  • choose the subscribers to include inside an export. More information [here](#operation/Exports_Export)
📝 To create a new target, you first need to create a Target Object with this [POST method](#operation/Targets_Post). Then, depending on your targeting criteria, you need to create the right filter objects to assign to your Target ID. 💡 It is recommended to first read the API documentation [here](../en/docs/toolssimpletarget). You will find an example of target creation.
